cards.explanation: The answer is peace, friends! Paul says that since we have been justified through faith, "…we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ…" Notice he says "we have," not "we might get some someday." It's already in the box.
The answer is False, friends. Paul says we have gained access "…by faith into this grace in which we stand." He never says we got in by working hard enough. That access comes through Jesus.
The word is hope, friends. Paul says, "And we rejoice in the hope of the glory of God." That comes right after he says we stand in this grace, so we're not rejoicing from shaky ground.

The answer is our sufferings, friends. Paul says, "Not only that, but we also rejoice in our sufferings…" I know, I did a double take too. He doesn't say suffering feels good. He says we rejoice in it because of what we know it produces.
The word is perseverance, friends. Paul says, "…we know that suffering produces perseverance…" That's the reason he gives for rejoicing. It's the first link in his chain.
The answer is True, friends! Paul says, "…perseverance, character; and character, hope." So the chain runs from suffering to perseverance to character to hope. And hope is where he lands.

The reason is that God has poured out His love into our hearts, friends. Paul says, "…hope does not disappoint us, because God has poured out His love into our hearts…" The hope rests on God's love, and Paul says that love has already been poured out into our hearts.

The answer is the Holy Spirit, friends! Paul says God has poured out His love into our hearts "…through the Holy Spirit, whom He has given us." So the Spirit is a gift God has given. That's a lot of good packed into one verse.
The word is ungodly, friends. Paul says, "…while we were still powerless, Christ died for the ungodly." Christ didn't wait for us to get strong first. He died for us while we were powerless.

The answer is False, friends. Paul says, "Very rarely will anyone die for a righteous man, though for a good man someone might possibly dare to die." Very rarely is not common. That sets up how much bigger verse 8 is.

The answer is that Christ died for us while we were still sinners, friends. Paul says, "But God proves His love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us." The proof came while we were still sinners. We weren't cleaned up first, and Christ died for us anyway.

The answer is True, friends. Paul says, "Therefore, since we have now been justified by His blood, how much more shall we be saved from wrath through Him!" I think Paul is excited here, and I would be too. We've been justified by His blood, and we'll be saved from wrath through Him.

The answer is the death of His Son, friends. Paul says, "…if, when we were enemies of God, we were reconciled to Him through the death of His Son…" Reconciled means brought back together. He did that for us when we were enemies.

The word is life, friends. Paul says, "…how much more, having been reconciled, shall we be saved through His life!" We were reconciled through His death, and saved through His life. Paul is stacking it up.

The answer is God Himself, friends. Paul says, "…we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation." We rejoice in God, and it all comes through Jesus.
